facts.text: A sensor is a device that measures something about the world, such as distance, light or speed, and converts the measurement into an electrical signal a computer can read.
facts.quote: A sensor is a device that measures something about the world, such as distance, light or speed, and turns the measurement into an electrical signal a computer can read.

facts.text: Sensors relevant to a collision system must establish whether something is near the machine, where the object is and how fast the object is moving.
facts.quote: The sensors that matter for a collision system answer one question: is there something near the machine, where is it, and how fast is it moving?

facts.text: Sensor types use different physical principles, so each performs well in some conditions and is blind in others.
facts.quote: Each sensor type works on a different physical principle, so each is good in some conditions and blind in others.

facts.text: Cooperative sensing systems require a tag on every person or vehicle.
facts.quote: "cooperative" systems that need a tag on every person or vehicle [Chapter 6]

facts.text: Sensor behavior in dust, fog and darkness must be distinguished from how well that behavior can be simulated.
facts.quote: The dust, fog and darkness columns describe how the sensor itself behaves, which the booklet treats separately from how well that behavior can be simulated [Chapter 6].

facts.text: A camera measures visible light as a flat color image, providing rich detail that can distinguish a person from a post at low cost.
facts.quote: Camera | Visible light as a flat color image | Rich detail; can tell a person from a post; cheap

facts.text: Camera performance in dust is weak because dust hides objects and coats the lens.
facts.quote: Weak: dust hides objects and coats the lens; simulated only as haze overlays

facts.text: Camera dust effects are simulated only as haze overlays.
facts.quote: dust hides objects and coats the lens; simulated only as haze overlays

facts.text: Camera performance in fog is weak to partial because image contrast falls as fog density increases.
facts.quote: Weak to partial: contrast falls with density; the best-reproduced camera condition in simulation

facts.text: Fog is the best-reproduced camera condition in simulation.
facts.quote: the best-reproduced camera condition in simulation

facts.text: Camera performance in darkness is weak because cameras need light and image noise increases in the dark.
facts.quote: Weak: needs light; noise rises in the dark; night is the hardest condition for generated images

facts.text: Night is the hardest camera condition for generated images.
facts.quote: night is the hardest condition for generated images

facts.text: Lidar measures distance to many points using laser time of flight and also measures return strength, or intensity; lidar provides precise long-range 3D geometry and works day and night.
facts.quote: Lidar | Distance to many points from laser time of flight, plus return strength (intensity) | Precise 3D geometry at long range; works day and night

facts.text: Lidar performance in dust is partial because dust scatters the beam, adding false returns and causing lost returns.
facts.quote: Partial: dust scatters the beam, adding false and lost returns

facts.text: Four distinct lidar behaviors have been seen in field dust, and lidar behavior in dust is identified as the biggest off-road gap.
facts.quote: four distinct behaviors seen in field dust; the biggest off-road gap

facts.text: Lidar performance in fog is partial to good: attenuation and backscatter are well studied, but dense fog remains difficult.
facts.quote: Partial to good: attenuation and backscatter well studied; dense fog still hard

facts.text: Lidar performance in darkness is good and largely unaffected apart from background light.
facts.quote: Good: largely unaffected apart from background light

facts.text: Radar measures distance and closing speed from radio echoes in the 77 GHz band and measures speed directly.
facts.quote: Radar | Distance and closing speed from radio echoes (77 GHz band) | Largely unaffected by airborne dust, fog and darkness; measures speed directly

facts.text: Radar sees shapes coarsely and can be confused by metal.
facts.quote: but it sees shapes coarsely and is confused by metal.

facts.text: Radar measurements show little effect from airborne dust, but the effect of dust caking the radar cover remains an open question.
facts.quote: Good: measurements show little effect from airborne dust; dust caking the cover is a separate open question

facts.text: Ordinary fog has only a minor effect on radar, and darkness does not affect radar.
facts.quote: Good: ordinary fog has minor effect | Not affected

facts.text: Ultrasonic sensors measure distance to the nearest surface over a few meters using sound echoes; ultrasonic sensors are cheap and perform well at very close range.
facts.quote: Ultrasonic | Distance to the nearest surface over a few meters, from sound echoes | Cheap; good at very close range; ignores light

facts.text: Ultrasonic sensor performance in dust is unknown because no validation was found; contamination and rough surfaces are weak points.
facts.quote: Unknown: no validation found; contamination and rough surfaces are weak points

facts.text: Ultrasonic sensor performance in fog is weak and weakly evidenced, with behavior dependent on temperature and humidity.
facts.quote: Weak: depends on temperature and humidity; weakly evidenced

facts.text: Ultrasonic sensors ignore light and are unaffected by darkness.
facts.quote: Cheap; good at very close range; ignores light

facts.text: Thermal cameras measure heat radiation in the long-wave infrared band as an image and can see warm people and engines without light.
facts.quote: Thermal camera | Heat radiation (long-wave infrared) as an image | Sees warm people and engines without light

facts.text: Thermal camera performance in dust is weak and depends on particle size and temperature; no validation was found.
facts.quote: Weak: particle size and temperature matter; no validation found

facts.text: Thermal camera performance in fog is weak because moisture absorbs infrared; no off-road validation was found.
facts.quote: Weak: moisture absorbs infrared; no off-road validation

facts.text: Thermal camera performance in darkness is partial: thermal cameras work without light, but image contrast depends on temperature differences.
facts.quote: Partial: works without light, but contrast depends on temperature differences

facts.text: Lidar has ranged to a retroreflective target through dust with only 2% light transmission, and to a dark target with only 6% light transmission.
facts.quote: Lidar has ranged to a target through dust with only 2% light transmission (a retroreflective target) or 6% (a dark one) [Chapter 6].

facts.text: A tractor-mounted lidar's position error increased by up to 27% with speed.
facts.quote: A tractor-mounted lidar's position error rose by up to 27% with speed

facts.text: A stabilizer reduced a tractor-mounted lidar's average position error by 57%, from 382 mm to 161 mm.
facts.quote: a stabilizer cut the average error by 57%, from 382 mm to 161 mm [Chapter 6].

facts.text: The sensor types for the new collision mitigation system were unconfirmed when the booklet was written; every later step depends on the sensor choice, creating a schedule risk.
facts.quote: The sensor types for the new system were not confirmed when the booklet was written, and every later step depends on that choice; the booklet calls this a schedule risk

facts.text: Sensor-model and data requirements should be written into the sourcing contract now.
facts.quote: recommends writing sensor-model and data requirements into the sourcing contract now [Chapter 6].

facts.text: The combination of sensors and disagreements between sensors must be validated because no sensor performs well in every condition.
facts.quote: No sensor is good in every condition, so the combination of sensors, and the disagreement between them, is itself part of what must be validated [Chapters 1, 6].
